findings.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py does not implement the abstract methods (build_occurrence_and_event_data, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values) required by its new StatefulDetectorHandler base class, causing TypeError on instantiation in production paths when a METRIC_ALERT detector reaches handler_cls(detector)

The new @abc.abstractmethod build_occurrence_and_event_data is placed on the base DetectorHandler class instead of StatefulDetectorHandler, breaking other existing DetectorHandler subclasses (e.g. MockDetectorHandler in tests) that will now fail at instantiation even though the method is meaningless for their evaluate()-only flow

In evaluate_group_key_value, replacing 'result = None' with a type annotation 'result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence' makes the annotation claim non-optional while downstream code still checks 'result is not None', and any future added branch could cause UnboundLocalError instead of an intended None

PriorityLevel(new_status) in evaluate_group_key_key_value's new else branch assumes value parity between DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel enums; if they drift, ValueError will abort the whole packet's evaluation

Duplicate group-key handling changed from logging an error and keeping both results to silent last-write-wins overwriting in evaluate(), so the first group's occurrence is silently dropped with no signal
Test coverage gap: tests use hardcoded value=6 in expected occurrences regardless of actual group values (8, 10, 100), so value propagation to the build hook is not verified

Unbounded per-group-key fan-out of synchronous Kafka produces: each changed group key triggers a full IssueOccurrence + event payload and an individual produce_occurrence_to_kafka call with no batching, rate limiting, or cap, risking consumer lag and memory pressure (detector.py ~234-245 and process_detectors ~55-60)

No backpressure/ordering guarantee between occurrence production and commit_state_updates: occurrences are produced to Kafka inside the loop but dedupe/state updates are only committed afterwards, so mid-loop worker failure causes all occurrences to replay on retry, duplicating Kafka load and issue occurrences

MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) it does not implement, so instantiation raises TypeError and detector_handler construction fails at evaluation time for every metric-alert detector
Per-key Redis write pattern in commit_state_updates without batching: reads are chunked/pipelined but writes are done per-key, causing N Redis round-trips on the write side for many group keys

Expected occurrences in tests are built with hardcoded value=6 (e.g. test_dedupe uses value=6 while data packet uses {"val1": 8}; test_results_on_change uses 100 in packet but 6 in expected; test_state_results_multi_group uses 10 for group_2 but 6 in expected), and build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value argument, so value propagation via evaluate_group_key_value to build_occurrence_and_event_data is never verified and the new value parameter has zero behavioral coverage

No test of the resolution/status-change path through process_detectors: tests only assert PayloadType.OCCURRENCE and there is no test that a detector transitioning to OK results in produce_occurrence_to_kafka called with PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE and the correct StatusChangeMessage

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with abstract build_occurrence_and_event_data but has an empty pass body, so instantiating it raises TypeError; no test exercises a detector with type=MetricAlertDetector.slug, so the breakage will only be discovered in production
The deleted test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was not replaced with equivalent coverage: the new process_detectors contract's overwrite/dedup semantics for duplicate group keys has no test

New Detector.group_type property (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:58) returning grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type) has no direct test (valid slug, invalid slug → None); only exercised incidentally

test_state_results_multi_group uses assert_has_calls without asserting call count, so a double-produce for one group would still pass; adding mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.call_count == 2 would close this gap

MetricAlertDetectorHandler in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py has a pass-only body and inherits unimplemented abstract methods (including build_occurrence_and_event_data), causing TypeError when constructed; the TODO warning comment was also removed

build_occurrence_and_event_data is declared abstract on the wrong class (DetectorHandler instead of StatefulDetectorHandler), forcing stateless detector handlers to implement an occurrence-building hook they don't use
import builtins / builtins.type[GroupType] annotation in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py is an unnecessary non-idiomatic type-boundary workaround; the field should be renamed instead
Test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event re-implements production occurrence/event construction with hardcoded identity fields (id and event_id), risking drift and ID collisions

Test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value parameter, masking whether the correct group value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data and giving false confidence in the new hook's wiring

assert_updates tri-state None-vs-check protocol is fragile: callers pass None to mean absent but legitimate (None, HIGH) states can't be asserted, and the ambiguity is now baked into every detector test

MetricAlertDetectorHandler is uninstantiable: it subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing abstract methods build_occurrence_and_event_data, get_dedupe_value, and get_group_key_values, causing TypeError on instantiation and crashing process_detectors for all detectors in the batch

Test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value parameter, so tests like test_state_results_multi_group, test_results_on_change, and test_dedupe pass even when evaluate_group_key_value passes the wrong value into build_occurrence_and_event_data

Kafka produce happens before detector state commit in process_detectors with no rollback: if produce fails, state updates are never committed causing duplicate occurrences on redelivery; if commit fails after produce, the detector fires again despite the issue already reported

Duplicate-group-key error log was removed and test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was deleted rather than adapted, and process_detectors return type changed from list to dict without updating any callers, potentially breaking consumers that unpack a list[DetectorEvaluationResult]
PriorityLevel(new_status) conversion in evaluate_group_key_value can raise for unmapped enum levels, leaving enqueued-but-inconsistent in-memory state with a partially-processed packet

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py does not implement the abstract methods (build_occurrence_and_event_data, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values) required by its new StatefulDetectorHandler base class, causing TypeError on instantiation in production paths when a METRIC_ALERT detector reaches handler_cls(detector)

The new @abc.abstractmethod build_occurrence_and_event_data is placed on the base DetectorHandler class instead of StatefulDetectorHandler, breaking other existing DetectorHandler subclasses (e.g. MockDetectorHandler in tests) that will now fail at instantiation even though the method is meaningless for their evaluate()-only flow

adjudication.rationale: `build_occurrence_and_event_data` is added as an `@abc.abstractmethod` on `StatefulDetectorHandler` (it appears immediately after `get_group_key_values`, which is a `StatefulDetectorHandler` abstract method), not on the base `DetectorHandler`. The base `DetectorHandler` still only defines the abstract `evaluate(...)`. Accordingly, existing `DetectorHandler` subclasses like `MockDetectorHandler` in the tests are not required to implement `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and the diff updates `MockDetectorHandler.evaluate` without adding that method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In evaluate_group_key_value, replacing 'result = None' with a type annotation 'result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence' makes the annotation claim non-optional while downstream code still checks 'result is not None', and any future added branch could cause UnboundLocalError instead of an intended None

adjudication.rationale: In `evaluate_group_key_value`, the local `result` variable is always assigned on all paths that reach the `DetectorEvaluationResult` construction: either `new_status == DetectorPriorityLevel.OK` assigns a `StatusChangeMessage`, or the `else` assigns from `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)`. If there is no status change, the function returns `None` before reaching the annotated variable. The downstream `if result.result is not None` check refers to `DetectorEvaluationResult.result`, not this local variable, and the diff does not introduce an `UnboundLocalError` risk on any current branch; concerns about “future added branch” are speculative and not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PriorityLevel(new_status) in evaluate_group_key_key_value's new else branch assumes value parity between DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel enums; if they drift, ValueError will abort the whole packet's evaluation

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the new non-OK branch calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, PriorityLevel(new_status))`. Here `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel` (from `sentry.workflow_engine.types`), and the diff provides no guarantee that `DetectorPriorityLevel` values map 1:1 to `sentry.types.group.PriorityLevel`. If they ever diverge, `PriorityLevel(new_status)` can raise `ValueError`, and there is no local handling in `evaluate(...)`/`process_detectors(...)`, so the whole packet evaluation could error out. The diff doesn’t prove the enums currently differ, so it’s a robustness/contract concern rather than a verifiable present defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate group-key handling changed from logging an error and keeping both results to silent last-write-wins overwriting in evaluate(), so the first group's occurrence is silently dropped with no signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `DetectorHandler.evaluate`/`StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (so duplicate keys are not representable). In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, results are built by iterating `group_values.items()` where `group_values` is itself a `dict`, so duplicate group keys cannot occur in this path. While `process_detectors` previously logged an error on duplicate `result.group_key` values from a list, that scenario is effectively eliminated by the new dict-based API; there’s no verifiable case in the diff where a “first group’s occurrence is silently dropped” due to overwriting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test coverage gap: tests use hardcoded value=6 in expected occurrences regardless of actual group values (8, 10, 100), so value propagation to the build hook is not verified

Unbounded per-group-key fan-out of synchronous Kafka produces: each changed group key triggers a full IssueOccurrence + event payload and an individual produce_occurrence_to_kafka call with no batching, rate limiting, or cap, risking consumer lag and memory pressure (detector.py ~234-245 and process_detectors ~55-60)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` to return a dict of results keyed by group key, and `process_detectors` now iterates `for result in detector_results.values():` and calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` for every non-None `result.result` (see `processors/detector.py` around the modified loop). In `evaluate_group_key_value`, for non-OK transitions it now *builds* an `IssueOccurrence` plus `event_data` per group key via `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` and returns it in `DetectorEvaluationResult`. The tests explicitly assert `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` is called once per group key in multi-group cases. The diff shows no batching/capping/rate limiting in this path, so a packet with many group keys will synchronously fan out into many produce calls and payload constructions. This is a real, diff-grounded scalability/architecture concern rather than a correctness bug proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No backpressure/ordering guarantee between occurrence production and commit_state_updates: occurrences are produced to Kafka inside the loop but dedupe/state updates are only committed afterwards, so mid-loop worker failure causes all occurrences to replay on retry, duplicating Kafka load and issue occurrences

adjudication.rationale: In `process_detectors`, occurrences are produced immediately during iteration (`for result in detector_results.values(): ... create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)`), while `StatefulDetectorHandler` clearly separates state persistence into a later `commit_state_updates()` step (it enqueues updates during `evaluate_group_key_value` via `enqueue_state_update(...)` and exposes `commit_state_updates()` separately). `process_detectors` does not call `commit_state_updates()` at all in the shown diff, so there is no atomic/ordered coupling between producing to Kafka and persisting dedupe/state updates. That supports the review concern as a reliability/ordering issue (potential duplicate production on retry/crash), though the diff alone doesn’t prove the exact retry/worker-failure behavior end-to-end.

Per-key Redis write pattern in commit_state_updates without batching: reads are chunked/pipelined but writes are done per-key, causing N Redis round-trips on the write side for many group keys

There’s no diff-grounded evidence here that reads are pipelined/chunked while writes are per-key, or that this PR introduced/exposed N extra Redis round-trips on the write side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test of the resolution/status-change path through process_detectors: tests only assert PayloadType.OCCURRENCE and there is no test that a detector transitioning to OK results in produce_occurrence_to_kafka called with PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE and the correct StatusChangeMessage

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `process_detectors` now iterates `for result in detector_results.values():` and calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` whenever `result.result is not None` (which includes both `IssueOccurrence` and `StatusChangeMessage`, since `evaluate_group_key_value` sets `result = StatusChangeMessage(...)` when `new_status == DetectorPriorityLevel.OK`). The updated `TestProcessDetectors` adds assertions only for the occurrence path (patching `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` and asserting `payload_type=PayloadType.OCCURRENCE`, `status_change=None`), but there is no test exercising a transition to OK/resolution through `process_detectors` and verifying a STATUS_CHANGE production with the correct `StatusChangeMessage`. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing test for a meaningful path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with abstract build_occurrence_and_event_data but has an empty pass body, so instantiating it raises TypeError; no test exercises a detector with type=MetricAlertDetector.slug, so the breakage will only be discovered in production
The deleted test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was not replaced with equivalent coverage: the new process_detectors contract's overwrite/dedup semantics for duplicate group keys has no test

adjudication.rationale: In this diff the detector handler contract changes from returning a list to returning a dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey` (`DetectorHandler.evaluate` and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`). With this contract, duplicate group keys cannot be represented in the returned structure (a dict can only have one value per key), and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` iterates `group_values.items()` where `group_values` is itself a `dict[str, int]`, so duplicate keys are already impossible at that stage. The prior duplicate-detection logic in `process_detectors` (and the corresponding `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe`) was removed because duplicates are structurally eliminated, not because new dedup/overwrite logic was added that needs testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New Detector.group_type property (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:58) returning grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type) has no direct test (valid slug, invalid slug → None); only exercised incidentally

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `Detector.group_type` property that wraps `grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type)` and then refactors `detector_handler` to use it. In the updated tests, the behavior is exercised only indirectly (e.g., `test_no_issue_type` drives `process_detectors` which calls `detector.detector_handler` → `self.group_type`, and `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` asserts `handler.detector.group_type is not None`), but there is no direct, explicit test of `Detector.group_type` returning a `GroupType` for a valid slug and `None` for an invalid slug. This is a concrete “missing focused test for newly added API” issue, not a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_state_results_multi_group uses assert_has_calls without asserting call count, so a double-produce for one group would still pass; adding mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.call_count == 2 would close this gap

adjudication.rationale: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the test uses `mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.assert_has_calls([...], any_order=True)` but does not assert the total number of calls (e.g., `call_count == 2`). `assert_has_calls` allows extra calls, so if the code produced an extra occurrence for one group (3 total calls) while still producing the two expected calls, the test would still pass. This is a test coverage/strictness gap introduced/visible in the diff, not a confirmed product defect.

This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: build_occurrence_and_event_data is declared abstract on the wrong class (DetectorHandler instead of StatefulDetectorHandler), forcing stateless detector handlers to implement an occurrence-building hook they don't use

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` is added as an `@abc.abstractmethod` on the base `DetectorHandler` class (near the existing abstract hooks), not on `StatefulDetectorHandler`. That means any stateless `DetectorHandler` subclass must implement it to be instantiable. The diff still defines a stateless `MockDetectorHandler(DetectorHandler[dict])` in tests that only implements `evaluate(...)` and does not implement `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, so with this signature as abstract on `DetectorHandler`, instantiating such handlers would fail with an ABC TypeError. This matches the finding that the abstract method is on the wrong class and forces unused implementation on stateless handlers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import builtins / builtins.type[GroupType] annotation in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py is an unnecessary non-idiomatic type-boundary workaround; the field should be renamed instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `import builtins` and annotates `group_type` as `builtins.type[GroupType] | None` in `src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py`, but nothing in the diff shows this causes incorrect behavior or a concrete reviewable problem. Whether `builtins.type[...]` is “non-idiomatic” or whether the model field should be renamed is a stylistic/architectural preference not verifiable as a defect or necessary change from the PR content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event re-implements production occurrence/event construction with hardcoded identity fields (id and event_id), risking drift and ID collisions

adjudication.rationale: In tests, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` constructs an `IssueOccurrence` directly and hardcodes identity-like fields (`id="eb4b0acffadb4d098d48cb14165ab578"`, `event_id="43878ab4419f4ab181f6379ac376d5aa"`) while also manually assembling `event_data`. This is a diff-grounded maintainability concern: the helper is effectively re-creating occurrence/event payload structure rather than using a shared factory/fixture, which can drift as production expectations evolve. However, nothing in the diff shows this causing a functional defect (the occurrence is not persisted/uniqueness-validated here), so it’s not a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value parameter, masking whether the correct group value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data and giving false confidence in the new hook's wiring

adjudication.rationale: In tests, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, group_key, value, new_status)` accepts a `value` argument but does not use it when constructing the `IssueOccurrence` or `event_data` (it only uses `group_key`, `new_status`, and handler-derived fields). Since `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` now calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, ...)`, these tests can’t actually validate that the correct `value` is being passed through the new hook, potentially giving false confidence in the wiring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: assert_updates tri-state None-vs-check protocol is fragile: callers pass None to mean absent but legitimate (None, HIGH) states can't be asserted, and the ambiguity is now baked into every detector test

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `assert_updates` uses `None` as a sentinel meaning “don’t assert / expect absence” for `dedupe_value`, `counter_updates`, `active`, and `priority`. But the state being asserted (`handler.dedupe_updates`, `handler.counter_updates`, `handler.state_updates`) is populated with non-`None` values in this change: dedupe values are `int`, counter updates are `dict`/numbers, and state updates are `(bool, DetectorPriorityLevel)`. A “legitimate (None, HIGH) state” is not shown as a possible/produced value; `group_key` being `None` is supported because it’s just a dict key and is not part of the sentinel protocol. So the finding isn’t verifiable from this diff and reads as hypothetical rather than a concrete issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is uninstantiable: it subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing abstract methods build_occurrence_and_event_data, get_dedupe_value, and get_group_key_values, causing TypeError on instantiation and crashing process_detectors for all detectors in the batch

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` but is defined as `pass`, so it does not implement the abstract methods added/required on `StatefulDetectorHandler` (`get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). That makes the class abstract/uninstantiable and would raise `TypeError` when `Detector.detector_handler` tries to construct the handler for a detector whose grouptype uses this handler. `process_detectors` does not catch such exceptions, so a single such detector would abort processing for the batch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value parameter, so tests like test_state_results_multi_group, test_results_on_change, and test_dedupe pass even when evaluate_group_key_value passes the wrong value into build_occurrence_and_event_data

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/.../test_detector.py`, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., value, ...)` never uses the `value` argument when constructing the `IssueOccurrence` or `event_data` (it only uses `group_key`, handler fingerprint, timestamps, etc.). This makes the tests unable to assert that `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` passes the correct `value` into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. This is visible in `test_state_results_multi_group`, where the second group has `group_vals: {"group_2": 10}` but the expected occurrence is built with `value=6`; the test still passes because `value` is ignored. This is a test-quality/coverage gap rather than a verifiable production defect in the diff (the implementation does pass `value` through).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Kafka produce happens before detector state commit in process_detectors with no rollback: if produce fails, state updates are never committed causing duplicate occurrences on redelivery; if commit fails after produce, the detector fires again despite the issue already reported

adjudication.rationale: In `process_detectors`, results are evaluated and then `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` is invoked immediately for each non-`None` result (`for result in detector_results.values(): ...`). The stateful handler path enqueues state updates inside `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` via `self.enqueue_state_update(...)`, but this diff does not show any corresponding `handler.commit_state_updates()` call in `process_detectors`, nor any error-handling/transaction boundary around producing vs committing. With this diff, detectors now generate occurrences on non-OK status via `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)`, increasing the risk of inconsistent side effects if production fails or if state commit happens elsewhere and fails. However, the diff alone does not prove when/where commits happen in the broader pipeline, so the "before commit" ordering/rollback claim isn’t fully verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-group-key error log was removed and test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was deleted rather than adapted, and process_detectors return type changed from list to dict without updating any callers, potentially breaking consumers that unpack a list[DetectorEvaluationResult]

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the duplicate-group-key detection/logging in `process_detectors` (it no longer builds a `detector_group_keys` set and now consumes `detector_results.values()`), and `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` was deleted rather than rewritten. The return types also clearly changed from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` in both `DetectorHandler.evaluate`/`StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` and `process_detectors`. However, the claim that callers were not updated cannot be verified from this diff alone (tests shown were updated), so this is best treated as an API/compatibility review concern rather than a proven defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PriorityLevel(new_status) conversion in evaluate_group_key_value can raise for unmapped enum levels, leaving enqueued-but-inconsistent in-memory state with a partially-processed packet

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the code enqueues state updates (`self.enqueue_state_update(...)`) before calling `PriorityLevel(new_status)` when building an occurrence (`build_occurrence_and_event_data(..., PriorityLevel(new_status))`). If `DetectorPriorityLevel` is not always a valid constructor input for `PriorityLevel`, that conversion would raise mid-evaluation, leaving the handler’s in-memory `*_updates` queues partially populated for a partially-processed packet. The diff doesn’t show the enum definitions, so the mismatch/raise isn’t verifiable here, but the new direct cross-enum cast is a concrete fragility introduced by this change.
